summary: The EXECUTED artifact-binding declaration on agent_templates (cinatra#3208). ONE additive nullable column: artifact_bindings text (JSON-as-text, the gated_steps / lifecycle_config convention), three-valued ON PURPOSE like has_artifact_bindings — it carries the normalized outputs[].cinatra.artifact bindings the compile that produced THIS template version actually found plus the typed cinatra.produces refs they were validated against (grammar, serializer and fail-closed parser in packages/agents/src/artifact-binding.ts); null = unknown, meaning a row compiled before this column existed or a compile that could not see its sibling package.json (binding/produces parity never established). WHY: run completion materialized a run's artifacts by re-reading the PACKAGE REGISTRY for the run's (package_name, package_version) pair while execution was bound to the immutable template-version snapshot on this row — two authorities with nothing binding them together, so a registry copy that had drifted from the copy the template was compiled from failed the run on a binding it never declared, after all the model work was done. The run-completion materializer (src/lib/artifacts/run-artifact-materializer.ts) now reads THIS column under the same version-pin guard has_artifact_bindings already uses and does not call the registry at all when it resolves; the registry read survives only as the unknown-row fallback, preserving cinatra#2497's wholesale classification and cinatra#2486's fail-closed posture exactly. Written ONLY together with package_version, in one statement, by every install/recompile writer — the version-pin guard is worthless if the two land in separate writes. No backfill, no rewrite, no constraint change: every existing row reads NULL ('unknown'), the same registry-reading fail-closed behavior every row had before this column existed — the repo's standing pre-release no-backward-compat convention; the choice to skip a backfill is recorded here and in the PR body. Idempotent ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL in buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries (src/lib/drizzle-store.ts), shipped in the SAME PR (core__0091 precedent). down() drops the column (run completion reverts to the pre-#3208 posture and can again materialize against a declaration the run did not execute). SEQ IS PROVISIONAL: assigned at merge — shipped max on origin/main at build time is core__0100; a concurrent lane may claim 0101 first, in which case renumber-at-merge is normal. migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
